questions.scenario: When you were a kid, what was your favorite way to play with toys?

options.text: Stacking blocks to build the tallest towers and bridges.
Playing with Hot Wheels, toy cars, and spinning gears.
Playing with battery-operated toys and snap-circuits.
Flying toy helicopters or playing with remote-control robots.
Mixing different slimes, kinetic sand, or chemistry sets to see how they react.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Something breaks in your house. What do you enjoy fixing the most?

options.text: Fixing a broken wooden chair or a cracked wall.
Fixing a jammed bicycle chain or a noisy fan motor.
Fixing a broken charging cable or changing a blown fuse.
Fixing a broken drone wing or a smart-home gadget.
Using strong glue, resin, or chemical solvents to perfectly seal and bond broken pieces together.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You are watching a Hollywood action movie. What catches your attention?

options.text: The massive, beautiful skyscrapers and futuristic city designs.
The high-speed car chases and the sound of heavy engines.
The giant glowing energy cores and lightning strikes.
The spaceships dogfighting or giant mecha-robots battling.
The massive explosions, chemical reactions, and melting metals in a factory.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you had to choose a school science experiment, what would you build?

options.text: A strong bridge made out of ice-cream sticks that can hold heavy weights.
A fast car powered by rubber bands or a mousetrap.
A lemon battery that can actually light up an LED bulb.
A pressurized water rocket that shoots high into the sky.
A bubbling volcano eruption using baking soda, vinegar, and red dye.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you look outside while traveling, what fascinates you the most?

options.text: How massive pillars support huge flyovers and bridges.
How the gears, wheels, and engines of trains or sports cars work.
How massive wind turbines or solar panels generate energy.
Airplanes taking off or looking at the stars and satellites at night.
The giant oil refineries, chemical plants, or water treatment facilities.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What do you usually end up drawing or doodling in the back of your notebook?

options.text: 3D houses, room layouts, or cool building designs.
Sports bikes, monster trucks, or mechanical gears.
Lightning bolts, neon circuits, or power grids.
Rockets, UFOs, or advanced Transformer-like robots.
Bubbling flasks, molecular structures, or glowing radioactive symbols.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you were given a superpower, what would you choose?

options.text: The power to instantly build a strong fortress out of thin air.
The power to run at the speed of a sports car.
The power to shoot, absorb, and control electricity.
The power to fly into space or control robots with my mind.
The power to manipulate elements, like turning water into solid ice or metal into liquid.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every physical job has a 'frustrating' part. Which of these are you okay dealing with?

options.text: Measuring the exact angles and lengths of a wall 10 times so it's perfect.
Getting my hands covered in black grease and oil while tightening bolts.
Carefully untangling and connecting dozens of tiny, dangerous wires.
Waiting hours to calibrate a sensor perfectly so the machine doesn't crash.
Wearing heavy safety gear while measuring exact drops of strong, smelling chemicals.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You go to a massive Amusement Park. Which ride is your favorite?

options.text: The giant Ferris wheel, because of its massive steel structure.
The extreme roller coaster, because of its crazy speed and tracks.
The bumping cars, where you see electric sparks touching the roof.
The Zero-Gravity drop tower or VR space simulator.
The 4D special effects shows featuring real fire explosions and colored smoke.
None of these.

questions.scenario: If you are part of a superhero team, what is your codename?

options.text: The Builder (Creates the ultimate base).
The Engine (Provides unstoppable physical force).
The Spark (Provides the raw energy).
The Pilot (Flies and controls the highest tech).
The Alchemist (Transforms matter and chemicals into powerful tools).
None of these.
